description:
This image presents a side-by-side comparison of two false-colour infrared satellite images, showcasing land cover change between 2006 (left) and 2012 (right). The predominant deep red hues in both images indicate dense, healthy vegetation, likely forest. Polygons delineate distinct land cover units, annotated with numeric labels.

In the 2006 image:
An upper section includes an area labelled "3110", appearing as dense vegetation. A lower, lighter-hued area of sparser vegetation is labelled "3400". Other, less clear labels such as "3330", "3310", and "3210" are also visible within other polygons.

In the 2012 image:
The area previously labelled "3110" in 2006 now shows distinct internal lighter patches, and parts of it have transitioned to be labelled "3400". The area previously labelled "3400" in 2006 remains labelled "3400". This visual change from "3110" to "3400" indicates forest clearing or regeneration. New darker, almost greyish, patches, possibly representing water bodies or shadowed areas, are more prominent within some polygons in the 2012 image, particularly in the upper left. Other less clear labels ("3330", "3310", "3210") remain visible.

Based on the surrounding document's context, which discusses "Forest clear-cuts" and "Transitional woodland", the class "3110" likely represents a forest area, and "3400" represents a clear-cut area, regenerating forest, or transitional woodland-shrub resulting from clear-cutting, demonstrating land use/land cover change (LULUC).
